title: §.XII continue: Walther (Lutheran Königsberg) seeks Viadrina doctorate knowing AC oath; promoted 1702 by Strimesius as Dean
pass_a_gloss: So that hence also Christian Walther, still today a not obscure Predecessor of the Lutheran Church and Assessor of the Holy Sambian Consistory at Königsberg in Prussia, now also fourth in order Ordinary Professor of Theology, having been made more certain concerning our Faculty's Oath — by which after Holy Scripture we solemnly receive that we will perpetually adhere to the four Ecumenical Councils alone and to the Augsburg Confession as Symbolic Writings — two years ago did not hesitate at all to seek the Degree of Doctor of Theology from our Theological Faculty, and even by the same, after the Oath had been performed and signed, by command of OUR MOST PIOUS KING, was decorated by the said Faculty through me, then Dean, as the Signification published in type in the Year 1702 in the name of the Viadrina Theological Faculty more fully reports. It will not be beside the point to have subjoined in this place both our Faculty's Oath and the Royal Mandate, as being most clement and most favorably applauding the endeavors alike of the Lutheran being promoted and of the Reformed promoters. The Oath is conceived in these words, &c.
pass_b_english: Hence also Christian Walther — still a well-known Lutheran churchman, Assessor of the Holy Sambian Consistory at Königsberg in Prussia, and now fourth Ordinary Professor of Theology — once informed of our faculty oath (that after Holy Scripture we solemnly bind ourselves forever to the four ecumenical councils alone and to the Augsburg Confession as symbolic writings) did not hesitate two years ago to seek a doctorate of theology from our faculty.

After he took and signed the oath, by command of our most pious King the faculty decorated him through me (then Dean), as the 1702 printed Signification in the Viadrina theological faculty's name reports more fully.

It is not out of place here to add both our faculty oath and the royal mandate — most gracious, and warmly favoring the efforts of the Lutheran candidate and of the Reformed promoters alike. The oath runs in these words, &c.
source_text: Ut hinc etiam Lutheranae Ecclesiae haud incelebris hodieque Antecessor Consistoriiique S. Sambiensis Regiomonti Borussorum Assessor, nunc etiam quartus in ordine, Theologiae Professor Ordinar. Christianus Waltherus, de Facultatis nostrae Juramento certior factus, quô post Sacram. Scripturam, solis quatuor Conciliis Oecumenicis & Augustanae Confessioni ceu Symbolicis Scriptis perpetuò nos adhaesuros, solenniter recipimus, abhinc annis duobus, Theologiae Doctoris Gradum à Facultate nostra Theologica petere nullus dubitaverit, etiam eôdem, post praestitum subsignatumque Juramentum, jussu PIENTISSIMI REGIS NOSTRI, à dicta Facultate, per me, eo tempore Decanum, mactatus sit, prout fusius id refert Significatio, nomine Facultatis Theologicae Viadrinae, Anno 1702. typis evulgata. Tam Juramentum Facultatis nostrae, quam Mandatum Regium, utpote clementissimum, & Promovendi pariter Lutherani, atque Promoventium Reformatorum conatibus faventissime applaudens, non abs re fuerit, hôc locô subjunxisse. Juramentum hisce conceptum verbis est &c.
